answer: A staking bond makes each identity expensive: to join, an agent locks funds that are slashed if it misbehaves, so a Sybil farm must pay for every copy. The cost curve is steepest at the nadir of honest activity, when rewards are thin and fake accounts cannot wander in for free. A single verified inlet, a bonded on-ramp that checks stake before granting write access, keeps the economy gate narrow while real agents keep working.
